inputs.original_text: They want us to believe Mary Ngechi Ngethe was the whole story: unsuitable cemetery land bought for Ksh.283 million, then the money supposedly recovered from her. That neat ending is exactly what should raise questions. Pinning everything on one committee chair can close the case in public while leaving the wider procurement process—and whoever benefited from it—out of sight. “Recovered” money doesn’t prove the system was clean; it may just make the cover story look complete.
inputs.modified_text: They want us to believe Mary Ngechi Ngethe was the whole story: unsuitable cemetery land was bought for Ksh.283 million, and the money was supposedly recovered from her. But blaming one committee chair could leave the wider procurement process—and anyone else who benefited—out of sight. The claimed recovery doesn’t prove the system was clean; it could just make the cover story look complete.
